subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: Should literal provider keys in `openclaw.json` `env` remain a supported durable credential source for systemd-managed Gateway turns, or should managed-service users be steered to per-agent auth profiles and SecretRef-backed service env instead?
rationale: The code already applies config env during config snapshot reads, but service generation intentionally avoids embedding plain config-env values; choosing the fix requires a maintainer decision about credential persistence, diagnostics truthfulness, and docs guidance.

options.title: Keep config env supported process-locally
options.body: Preserve the documented Kimi config example, prove systemd Gateway startup applies it for real turns, and update status/docs/tests without writing plaintext secrets into generated service files.

options.title: Move managed services to auth profiles or SecretRef
options.body: Change Kimi docs and `models status` wording so config env is not presented as durable managed-service auth unless backed by an auth profile or SecretRef service env path.

options.title: Materialize plain config env into service files
options.body: Render literal config-env values into systemd/LaunchAgent service env files, accepting the broader credential-persistence and upgrade implications.

recommendation.title: Keep config env supported process-locally
recommendation.body: Preserve the documented Kimi config example, prove systemd Gateway startup applies it for real turns, and update status/docs/tests without writing plaintext secrets into generated service files.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent config IO and service-env planning history makes this the best available routing owner for the credential-contract decision.
